cells.tense: Here at the table, the structure has come down and what survived is being kept well.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Give what survived the clearing a slow unhurried hour, no progress check attached.
cells.core:
The collapse has already happened, and what's left is plain enough to work with. What you gave up for this is on the record same as the result, and nothing at this table needs defending. You can sit here without managing how much of you shows. A steady hand on what survived is all the maintenance required right now, and the cost of giving it is smaller than the cost of what came down.

That steadiness is the thing to keep. Whatever stayed upright after the drop — a habit, a commitment, a person, an account — give it your attention without a schedule and without a running tally of how it's going. An hour is enough. The room is quieter than it was, and quiet is what's sending the signal it sends.

cells.tense: Tomorrow has already been argued through; you are standing in a clearer place drafting its account.
cells.act: strike one thing from the list that does not serve
cells.ask: Strike one item from the running list you keep for this clearing, and don't replace it.
cells.core:
You're already past the clearing, into the version where you explain it — what you'll say when it comes up, how each telling lands, who gets which chapter. The script got finished before the room did. Under all of it, the thing is simply over, and no sentence is owed. Running clean, none of that is a speech: you cross the cleared ground and the telling arrives later, or doesn't, and either way nothing in you is waiting on an audience.

Take the list you're carrying — every account, defense, and next move — and drop one entry. One. Put the list on paper first if that helps you see which line can go, cross that line, and leave the space where it was. The clearing doesn't need a narrator.

cells.tense: You're still standing where a door closed behind you; no account of it was made.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Carry only your own portion of what this cost, and set down anything that belonged to someone else.
cells.core:
It came down, and nothing was said to anyone about it. You stood in the middle of that and took the quiet as the whole reply, so the effort went into storage and the finished thing went unmarked. You're carrying the entire weight of what it took, plus pieces that were not yours to lift. Anybody watching would say the door is shut, and you're still holding the frame.

For a week, put down what isn't yours to carry — the parts other people handed you, the parts you grabbed out of habit. Set one of those down and see what remains in your arms, because that's the load you actually signed for.

cells.tense: What cleared here is yours, and the account files it under someone else's hand.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Tend what you built here the way you'd tend something whose keeping is plainly in your hands.
cells.core:
Whatever came down, you took it down. The account reads otherwise — a lucky break, a hand from somewhere, someone else's timing, the season turning. You moved first and kept moving when it was dark, and that part is filed under a word that leaves you out of it. Clean, this is plain: you can set a hand on what you made and know it answers to you, no apology standing in front of it. Yours is split right now.

The act is small. Spend one stretch of care on the thing itself — water it, mend it, show up for it — the way you'd look after anything whose keeping depends on your hand. No one has to be told about it for it to be yours.

attempts.check: The record does not support the claim that what the person gave up is unseen by others; Honor states what is honored is their own recognition of it — an external acknowledgment that may or may not arrive. A reader could reasonably say the acknowledgment came long ago and went quiet, or that they never needed a witness, so the Too Little cell bends that rather than asserting isolation. The asks are each one small, self-contained act from the medicine list and survive being wrong about the person; the sentence that serves the writer more than them is any line that treats a cleared structure as proof of a satisfying ending. Every cell must also stay off the wire between Stewardship and the draw's own terms — no 'honor', 'recognition', 'witness', 'sacrifice' said on glass, no claim about how the group sees them, and the celebration stays a fact of their life, not a mood the cell assigns them.
